shots: EVERY MIND ON EARTH WAS GROWN.
AI THAT USES TOOLS AND WRITES CODE
MOTION DESIGN, SOUND DESIGN & CODE BY CLAUDE
subtitles: 1943. Two scientists model the brain's neurons as simple logic switches.
Enough signals in, and it fires. The first artificial neuron.
1950. Alan Turing asks: can machines think?
If you can't tell the machine from the person, what's the difference?
1956. A summer workshop at Dartmouth gives the field its name.
1958. The Perceptron learns from examples by adjusting its own weights.
The hype begins immediately.
1966. ELIZA mirrors your words back. People confide in it anyway.
1969. A book proves a single-layer perceptron can't even learn XOR.
Promises outrun results. Funding freezes.
It happens twice.
1986. Backpropagation sends the error backward, so hidden layers can learn.
1989. Convolutional networks learn to read handwritten zip codes.
1997. Deep Blue searches 200 million positions a second.
The world chess champion resigns.
2009. ImageNet: over 14 million images, labelled by hand.
2012. AlexNet, trained on two gaming GPUs, crushes the field.
2016. AlphaGo takes on Lee Sedol, one of the greatest Go players alive.
Move 37 looks like a mistake. It's genius. AlphaGo wins 4 to 1.
2017. The Transformer: every word attends to every other word at once.
Change one word, and what ‘it’ refers to changes with it.
Then came scale. GPT-3: 175 billion parameters.
2020. AlphaFold predicts how proteins fold.
2022. Diffusion models learn to create by removing noise.
November 30, 2022. ChatGPT reaches the public.
Then everything, everywhere, at once.
